summary: Convert a decoded Yuv420Image to a packed sRGB Image for image operations, previews, and AI.
parameters: image: nullable Yuv420Image, such as value from spql.mcap.read_video

color_assumption: optional literal string or NULL. Accepted values: bt709_full, bt709_limited, srgb_bt709_full, srgb_bt709_limited, bt601_625_full, bt601_625_limited, bt601_525_full, bt601_525_limited.
returns: Nullable Image with contiguous RGB8 pixels, usable by spql.ai.score and Studio image previews.
details: Use spql.image.to_rgb(v.value) when range, matrix, primaries, and transfer are present. To inspect metadata, project v.value.range AS color_range, v.value.matrix AS color_matrix, v.value.primaries AS color_primaries, v.value.transfer AS color_transfer from a bounded read_video query; omit the large pixel planes. Prefer the recording configuration when it establishes missing color metadata. For object presence, gripper occupancy, pose, or other tasks that do not require accurate color, proceed without asking the user when only primaries and/or transfer are missing and range/matrix are known: use the provisional profile mapping below, inspect representative converted frames, and continue the requested analysis if the visual evidence is usable. For matrix bt470bg choose bt601_625_full or bt601_625_limited; for smpte170m choose bt601_525_full or bt601_525_limited; for bt709 choose bt709_full or bt709_limited. Match the suffix to the observed range. This is a Studio policy for provisional analysis, not recovered source metadata or a claim that the matrix establishes primaries/transfer. Include the selected color_assumption as a result column and disclose the assumption in the final answer. Do not claim calibrated color or lighting measurements. If the task requires accurate color or quantitative brightness, range/matrix are also missing, or no documented provisional mapping applies, establish the recording profile or ask for clarification. H.264, yuvj420p, and resolution alone do not establish a profile. Never invent option names. bt709_* supplies BT.709 matrix, primaries, and transfer; srgb_bt709_* supplies BT.709 matrix/primaries with sRGB transfer; bt601_625_* supplies BT.470BG matrix/primaries with BT.709 transfer; bt601_525_* supplies SMPTE 170M matrix, primaries, and transfer. The _full or _limited suffix supplies the range. Assumptions fill absent fields only and never override existing metadata; unsupported explicit metadata still fails. Omitted or NULL color_assumption requires complete metadata. For example, with full range, bt470bg matrix, and missing primaries/transfer, a gripper-holding-object task should use spql.image.to_rgb(v.value, 'bt601_625_full') AS image and 'bt601_625_full' AS color_assumption, inspect representative images, and continue; do not stop solely to request the profile. Existing source metadata still takes precedence over the provisional profile. Metadata inspection alone does not complete an object-recognition task. Invalid names such as bt709, srgb, sRGB, rec709, rec.709, and rgb are not accepted; planning may succeed before execution rejects them. After such an error, consult these values and inspect metadata rather than trying spelling variants. This converts decoded pixels; it does not decode video, repair packets, or perform inference.

summary: Read the complete member population of an MCAP Dataset.
parameters: dataset: required literal string; Dataset name or spiral-dataset:<resource>:<version>:<data-revision> selector
returns: One row per member, including id (UUIDv7), source Blob, and bounded MCAP file statistics.
details: Use FROM spql.mcap.episodes('actual_dataset'). This is the cohort population, including members without the selected camera topic. Preserve these members when joining camera evidence. Inspect the relation schema before using file-statistic columns.

summary: Read one MCAP topic with its native message schema and member identity.
parameters: dataset: required literal string; Dataset name or exact spiral-dataset selector
topic: required literal string from the Dataset schema
variant: optional literal string; inspected schema fingerprint when the topic cannot unify losslessly
returns: id (UUIDv7), chunk_start_offset (UInt64), sample_ordinal (UInt32), log_time and publish_time (UInt64), sequence, channel_id, and value (schema-dependent message struct).
details: Use FROM spql.mcap.read_topic('actual_dataset', 'actual_topic', 'actual_variant'); arguments are literals, not per-row Blobs. foxglove.CompressedVideo value.data contains encoded packets and value.format identifies the codec. sample_ordinal is local to a chunk: it is not a stream-wide decode index, even if all its values happen to be unique. Zero does not prove a stream start or keyframe. Native message order within a member is determined by chunk_start_offset and sample_ordinal together. MCAP log_time is not automatically presentation time. Prefer read_video for decoded camera evidence.

summary: Read a foxglove.CompressedVideo H.264 MCAP topic as decoded YUV420 frames.
parameters: dataset: required literal string; Dataset name or exact spiral-dataset selector
topic: required literal string from the Dataset schema
variant: optional literal string; inspected schema fingerprint
returns: id (UUIDv7), log_time and publish_time (UInt64), chunk_start_offset (UInt64), sample_ordinal and frame_ordinal (UInt32), value (nullable Yuv420Image). Each row is a decoded frame.
details: Use FROM spql.mcap.read_video('actual_dataset', 'actual_topic', 'actual_variant'). Filter id and half-open log_time bounds to limit reads. The reader preserves packet order and decodes preceding parameter sets/keyframes and following GOP packets as support without emitting frames outside the requested bounds. Native log_time and publish_time remain attached to access units through decoder reordering; do not relabel them as inferred presentation time. Stable frame identity is id, chunk_start_offset, sample_ordinal, frame_ordinal. sample_ordinal counts packets within a chunk. frame_ordinal is a zero-based index within each packet/access unit and resets for each packet. It is not a video-wide frame number: frame_ordinal < 1 selects the first frame of every packet, and frame_ordinal % 30 = 0 does not sample every thirtieth video frame. For a diagnostic read, select one episode, filter a short half-open log_time interval from observed timestamps, order by log_time, chunk_start_offset, sample_ordinal, frame_ordinal, and LIMIT the output. LIMIT alone does not guarantee bounded decoding. For sampling across a video, establish temporal ordering within each episode and inspect the supported sampling/window functions; never use packet-local ordinals as global frame indexes. value is a decoded Yuv420Image with color metadata; do not call video.decode on it. Discover spql.image.to_rgb before passing it to Image-only operations or inspect_images. Raw Yuv420Image cells have no encoded image preview. Missing topics produce no frames. Unsupported codecs, missing random access, schema changes, and oversized GOPs fail explicitly. Validate and inspect a small bounded query before building a full-cohort analysis. Diagnostic SQL template (replace dataset, topic, variant, START_NS and END_NS with inspected values; choose a short interval for the selected episode): WITH e AS (SELECT id FROM actual_dataset ORDER BY id LIMIT 1) SELECT v.id, v.log_time, v.chunk_start_offset, v.sample_ordinal, v.frame_ordinal, v.value.range AS color_range, v.value.matrix AS color_matrix, v.value.primaries AS color_primaries, v.value.transfer AS color_transfer FROM spql.mcap.read_video('actual_dataset', 'actual_topic', 'actual_variant') v JOIN e ON v.id = e.id WHERE v.log_time >= START_NS AND v.log_time < END_NS ORDER BY v.log_time, v.chunk_start_offset, v.sample_ordinal, v.frame_ordinal LIMIT 3. This inspects metadata without inference. Once conversion succeeds, use the same bounds to select spql.image.to_rgb(v.value) AS image, with a documented assumption only if justified, and inspect those images before expanding the analysis. Temporal sampling recipe for nonnegative elapsed times: compute CAST((log_time - message_start_time) / 1000000000 AS BIGINT) AS sampled_second, then ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id, sampled_second ORDER BY log_time, chunk_start_offset, sample_ordinal, frame_ordinal), and filter that row number to 1 before RGB conversion and inference. Filter log_time >= message_start_time and use an inspected non-null episode start. Division alone yields fractional values and does not create whole-second buckets. Verify the selected timestamps and per-bucket counts in a small metadata-only query before scoring. This native cast was checked at 1.6 seconds, 1.999999999 seconds, and 2 seconds: buckets are 1, 1, and 2. Do not assume unqualified FLOOR syntax is supported; discover exact native function names for alternatives.

summary: Expand encoded MP4 media into supported stream descriptions.
parameters: media: EncodedMedia
returns: One normalized stream-description row per supported MP4 stream.
details: Use CROSS JOIN LATERAL spql.media.streams(input.media) stream. Inspect the output schema before selecting stream fields. No pixel decoding is performed.

summary: Expand an MP4 Blob into decode-order encoded sample rows.
parameters: blob: Blob
returns: Sample rows with container offsets, exact timing, sync status, and EncodedPacket values.
details: Use CROSS JOIN LATERAL spql.mp4.read(input.blob) sample. This reads container samples without decoding pixels. Inspect the output schema before selecting sample fields.

summary: Expand an MP4 Blob into track headers.
parameters: blob: Blob
returns: One track-header row per supported MP4 track.
details: Use CROSS JOIN LATERAL spql.mp4.tracks(input.blob) track. This does not decode samples. Inspect the output schema before selecting track fields.

summary: Read a Parquet relation with a schema resolved from its source.
parameters: path: required literal string
returns: Rows with the source Parquet schema.
details: Use FROM spql.parquet.read('actual_path'). The path must be available to the current project; do not invent a source path. Inspect the resolved schema before selecting columns.

summary: Generate integers in a half-open range.
parameters: overload 1: stop (Int64)
overload 2: start (Int64), stop (Int64)
returns: One value (Int64) per integer in [0, stop) or [start, stop).
details: Use CROSS JOIN LATERAL spql.range(input.start, input.stop) r for a range per input row. Null arguments or stop <= start produce no rows. The stop value is exclusive.

summary: Expand a video source and a native selection into frame references without decoding pixels.
parameters: source: StreamRef, EncodedMedia, or packet source from spql.video.from_packets
selection: FrameIndices, FrameSlice, or FrameTimes; FrameNeighborhood additionally supported for StreamRef and EncodedMedia, not packet sources
returns: request_index, requested_time, frame, time, duration. Selected frame references appear in request order, including duplicates.
details: Use CROSS JOIN LATERAL spql.video.frames(input.source, input.selection) f, then spql.video.decode(f.frame) when pixels are needed. f is a relation alias, not a frame value. Discover the native frame-selection constructors and use their exact signatures. A packet source requires original decode order, in-band SPS/PPS, and an initial IDR; frame selection does not repair an incorrectly assembled stream. Do not assume the same fixed frame index exists in every episode.

summary: Describe one video stream from packet descriptors; requires original decode order and codec configuration.
parameters: packets: list of structs with payload (binary or Blob), decode_index (unique Int64), optional presentation_time (nanosecond duration)
codec: string; supported value h264
framing: string; supported value annex_b
returns: A packet-backed video source usable with spql.video.frames and spql.video.frame_at.
details: Construction is lazy. Execution sorts descriptors by decode_index, and frame indexing reads packet headers. Uniqueness alone does not establish correct order. Preserve each member/camera stream separately, in original decode order, including in-band SPS/PPS and an initial IDR. sample_ordinal from an MCAP reader is chunk-local and cannot alone supply decode_index. No MCAP schema or timestamp mapping is inferred. Prefer the source-aware MCAP video reader for camera tasks. An UndefinedPicParamSetId error can result from incorrect assembly; it does not establish that the source lacks parameter sets.

summary: Expand encoded media or a stream into presentation-order frame references without pixel decoding.
parameters: interval overload: source (StreamRef or EncodedMedia), optional start/end (nanosecond duration), optional fps (Float64), optional keyframes (boolean)
times overload: source (StreamRef or EncodedMedia), times (list of nanosecond durations), optional mode (string)
returns: frame, time, duration; times overload additionally returns request_index and requested_time in request order, including duplicates.
details: Use CROSS JOIN LATERAL spql.video.read(input.source, ...) f, then decode f.frame if pixels are needed. Omit optional arguments unless a supported value is known. Packet-backed sources use video.frames instead.

summary: Read a Vortex relation with a schema resolved from its source.
parameters: path: required literal string
returns: Rows with the source Vortex schema.
details: Use FROM spql.vortex.read('actual_path'). The path must be available to the current project; do not invent a source path. Inspect the resolved schema before selecting columns.
